title.narrative: Strengthening Disaster Risk Governance and Recovery Capacities Strengthening Disaster Risk Governance and Recovery Capacities

description.narrative: The purpose of this contract is to provide the EU¿s financial contribution to UNDP and UNDRR to implement part of the 11th EDF Intra-ACP Natural Disaster Risk Reduction (CRIS number: FED/2018/041-233l). The overall impact that this Action seeks is to reduce the impact of disasters, including those related to climate change and biological hazards, and increase resilience in African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries. Through four outputs that are aligned to three of the four priorities of the Sendai Framework, this joint UNDP/UNDRR Project will strengthen disaster risk reduction capacities of ACP regional institutions, build risk governance capacity in ACP countries, and enhance recovery processes and community level action in order to save lives.

comment.narrative: Using the multirisk profile undertaken by IOM with funding from the EU UNDP Country Office CO identified 2 atrisk communes Kabezi and Nyabiraba within the urban area of Bujumbura. In December 2023 experts from UNDP organised and facilitated a 2day exercise which purpose was to raise awareness on the importance of adopting an integrated approach embedding DRR and CCA for land management and development hear from the communities what are the main risks and their evolution since the disaster risk profile has been done map existing initiatives and partners that are working on DRR and CCA in the area and discuss and plan through a participative process key activities that could be implemented through the project and scaleup existing efforts.The following key activities have been identified together with national and local authorities civil society and partners that already have projects in the area such as FAO WFP Red Cross UNFPA and GIZ Reforestation of watershed Bamboo planting on riversides affected by erosion Planting for fixating specific areas prone to landslides Cleaning of ravinesUNDP CO is now finalising the work plan with the communities and will soon engage procurement to buy the equipment and material and work with the actors on the ground for a sound and coordinated implementation.

description.narrative: The continuous improvement of risk governance capacity is critical to face the increasing exposure of populations and assets to natural hazards, including epidemics, exacerbated by environmental degradation, climate change, and unsustainable development practices. The political and economic imperative for DRR and CCA is often weak in the face of competing priorities and there is little integration across levels of governance and sectors to support riskinformed development. This is further compounded by the weak integration of risk considerations into development planning, processes and tools. The empirical basis forDRR and for the preparation and application of risk assessments is constrained by scarce or scattered data environments in riskprone and poor developing countries with inadequate technical expertise, resources and conflicting institutional mandates. Furthermore, the impacts of climate change on disaster risk and its integration in risk assessments is still a challenge.

comment.narrative: Multicountry establishment of advisory committee in each of the 5 countries that goes beyond the project implementationIn each of the project country the UNDP CO setup an advisory committee in charge of monitoring the project implementation and provide strategic guidance and support to overcome potential challenges. Representatives from the government the EU Delegation and UNDP cochair the committee in which other key institutions and partners can participate depending the context.In countries where the national platform for DRR is established and active the advisory committee is completely embedded into it to avoid duplication and multiplying coordination mechanisms. Since the project is adopting an integrated approach that incorporate DRR and CCA it helps in strengthening coherence within the existing mechanism.But most interestingly in countries where such platform is not active such as Cameroun or Togo the advisory committee serves as a concrete basis for a broader mechanism that is looking at concrete activities funded through this project. All important institutions contribute to the design and implementation of these activities creating ownership and whole of government approach integrating DRR and CCA.In Cameroun for example such advisory committee form a proper task force which is responsible for the operational and technical implementation of the project always looking at coordinating with other existing initiatives on DRR and CCA. 13 persons 5 women and 8 men from different institutions and organisations 5 ministries territorial administration finance economy planning and land management environment nature conservancy and sustainable development and scientific research and innovation 2 technical institutions in charge of data collection and management National Institute for Statistics and National Observatory on Climate Change parliamentary association civil society and private sector.
